   MINUTES
  MALIBU ARTS COMMISSION
  REGULAR MEETING
  JANUARY 23, 2024
  CITY HALL, MULTIPURPOSE ROOM
  9:00AM.

MEETING CALL TO ORDER

  Chair Lawrence called the meeting to order at 9:04 a.m.

ROLL CALL

  The following persons were recorded in attendance by the Recording Secretary:

  PRESENT: Chair Fireball Lawrence; Vice Chair Julia Holland; and Commissioners Lotte
  Cherin, Barry Haldeman, and Peter Jones (arrived at 9:09 a.m.)

  ABSENT: Ex-Officio Graeme Clifford

  ALSO PRESENT: Kristin Riesgo, Community Services Director; Amanda Rigali,
  Recreation Coordinator; and Brittany Saleaumua, Administrative Assistant

PLEDGE OF ALLEGIANCE

  Commissioner Cherin led the Pledge of Allegiance.

  Commissioner Cherin requested the Pledge of Allegiance to be removed from the meeting
  agenda if there were no objections from the Commission.

  Commissioner Haldeman inquired if the meeting start time could be pushed to 10:00 a.m.

  In response to Commissioners Cherin and Haldeman, Community Services Director
  Riesgo stated the Commission would need to adopt a new Resolution for the Rules of
  Procedure and Decorum for the conduct of Malibu Arts Commission meetings approving
  the removal of the Pledge of Allegiance and modifying the meeting start time.

CITY OF MALIBU VISION STATEMENT

  Community Services Director Riesgo read the City of Malibu Vision Statement.

APPROVAL OF AGENDA

MOTION  Commissioner Cherin moved, and Chair Lawrence seconded a motion to approve
  the agenda. The question was called, and the motion carried 4-0, Commissioner
  Jones absent.

REPORT ON POSTING OF AGENDA

  Administrative Assistant Saleaumua reported the meeting agenda was properly posted on
  January I 9, 2024.

ITEM 1.  CEREMONIAL/PRESENTATIONS

  A.  Update on Poetry Programs from Malibu Poet Laureate Nathan Hassell

  Poet Laureate Nathan Hassell provided an update on Caffeinated Verse, Ripple
  Effect Workshops, Poetry Jubilations, and the annual Poetry Summit.

  Commissioner Jones arrived at 9:09 a.m.

  In response to Commissioner Jones, Mr. Hassell stated an outdoor poetry reading
  at Malibu Village Books would be difficult due to the noise on Pacific Coast
  Highway.

  Chair Lawrence suggested hosting a one-day multi-seminar talk at Our Lady of
  Malibu and Malibu High School that would result in a poetry contest to create
  awareness of poetry amongst the students.

  In response to Chair Lawrence, Mr. Hassell stated poetry writing workshops take
  place at Malibu schools, and selected students are invited to read their poems at the
  Poetry Summit.

ITEM 2.A.  WRITTEN AND ORAL COMMUNICATIONS FROM THE PUBLIC

  None.

ITEM 2.B.  COMMISSION AD HOC COMMITTEE REPORTS

  I.  Arts in Education

  Community Services Director Riesgo stated poetry workshops at Malibu
  and Webster Elementary School began the week of January 22, 2024. She
  stated staff would edit the 2024 poetry anthology which would be available
  at the end of the school year.

  2.  Malibu Public Art Exhibitions

  Community Services Director Riesgo stated the Student Art Exhibition
  would be displayed from February 5 through March 6, 2024, and a closing
  reception would be on March I 0, 2024, at 11 :00 a.m.
   Malibu Arts Commission Regular Meeting
  Minutes of January 23, 2024
  Page 3 of7

  In response to Vice Chair Holland, Community Services Director Riesgo
  stated staff would contact Malibu High School to discuss a music
  component at the Student Art Exhibition closing reception.

  In response to Chair Lawrence, Community Services Director Riesgo stated
  the City accepted all art mediums for the Student Art Exhibition.

  Chair Lawrence thanked Vice Chair Holland for securing the artist for the
  Dick Van Dyke exhibition and Leigh McCloskey. He stated the Leigh
  McCloskey art exhibition opening reception would be on March 24, 2024.

  Vice Chair Holland stated the opening reception would include a Question-
  and-Answer session with Mr. McCloskey.

3.  Business and Community Outreach

  In response to Chair Lawrence, Community Services Director Riesgo stated
  Malibu Village Books would be required to obtain a Temporary Use Pennit
  (TUP) for an event that was beyond the normal operations of the bookstore.

  In response to Commissioner Jones, Community Services Director Riesgo
  stated six TUPs were allotted per parcel and the bookstore owner would
  have to work with the property owner to submit the TUP application.

  Chair Lawrence suggested contacting Malibu Village Bookstore to discuss
  a potential poetry event.

  In response to Commissioner Jones, Community Services Director Riesgo
  stated the City could not sell poetry anthology books, but donations could
  be accepted.

4.  Social Media

  Chair Lawrence stated he wanted to share Arts Commission social media
  posts and requested to be tagged in the posts.

  Community Services Director Riesgo stated staff would research the
  options for "tagging" Commissioners through the Hootsuite platform.

  In response to Chair Lawrence, Recreation Coordinator Rigali stated staff
  posted arts information on social media twice a week.

  A.  Malibu City Gallery Exhibition Schedule
  Recommended Action: Review and approve the Malibu Public Art Exhibitions Ad
  Hoc Committee's recommendation to feature artist Pep Williams.

  Community Services Director Riesgo presented the staff report.

  Chair Lawrence stated the Pep Williams exhibition featured lowrider vehicles.

  Commissioner Cherin suggested featuring a new artist since Mr. Williams had a
  previous exhibition at the Malibu City Gallery.

  Commissioner Haldeman suggested Richard Reiner as a potential solo artist.

  In response to Commissioner Haldeman, Chair Lawrence stated the last exhibition
  should include photography. He stated the artist selection process should include
  an evaluation of the work, history, and experience. He stated the Commission
  should provide artist suggestions for future shows.

  Commissioner Cherin requested additional time to contact potential artists and to
  review the exhibition schedule at the February 27, 2024 Regular meeting.

  Commissioner Jones stated the lowrider culture did not fit the Malibu culture.

  Chair Lawrence indicated disagreement with Commissioner Jones.

MOTION  Commissioner Haldeman moved, and Vice Chair Holland seconded a motion to
  continue Item 4.A. to the February 27, 2024 Regular meeting.

  Commissioner Jones stated artists should be selected by the Ad Hoc Committee.

  Commissioner Cherin indicated disagreement with Commissioner Jones.

  Chair Lawrence stated the Ad Hoc Committee completed an evaluation of each
  artist before it is presented to the Commission for approval. He stated the
  Commission had not provided the Ad Hoc Committee with suggested featured
  artists, and he encouraged the Commission to provide artist suggestions.

  In response to Commissioner Cherin, Community Services Director Riesgo stated
  Commissioners should provide the artist's name, contact information, and artwork
  examples by Febrnary 10, 2024.

FRIENDLY AMENDMENT
  Commissioner Cherin amended the motion for Commissioners to submit their artist
  recommendations to staff no later than February 10, 2024.

  Commissioner Haldeman accepted the amendment.

  The question was called, and the motion carried unanimously.

  Commissioner Cherin left the meeting at 10:21 a.m.

  B.  Guidelines for Temporary Public Art
  Recommended Action: 1) Review the draft guidelines for the temporary display of
  artwork; and 2) Provide feedback to staff.

  Community Services Director Riesgo presented the staff report.

  Commissioner Haldeman inquired about the Neighborhood Beautification Program
  discussed by the Public Works Commission.

  Commissioner Jones stated the guidelines should address sculptures.

  Administrative Assistant Saleaumua clarified the guidelines were for temporary
  artwork installations at City facilities. She stated it did not include permanent
  artwork or collections.

  Chair Lawrence requested additional time to review the draft guidelines. He
  requested to continue the item to the February 27, 2024 Regular meeting.

CONSENSUS
  By Consensus, the Commission agreed to review the draft guidelines for the
  temporary display of artwork for discussion at the February 27, 2024 Regular
  meeting.

  Commissioner Haldeman stated the exhibition item should be revised to note that

  Chair Lawrence suggested adding the number of exhibitions the Commission has

  Commissioner Jones stated the anthology should be included in the repmt stating

To:  Chair Lawrence and Members of the Arts Commission

Prepared by:  Kristin Riesgo, Community Services Director

Date prepared:  February 19, 2024  Meeting date: February 27, 2024

Subject:  Malibu City Gallery Exhibition Schedule

RECOMMENDED ACTION : Approve the Malibu Public Art Exhibitions Ad Hoc
Committee's recommendation to feature artist Pep Williams.

DISCUSSION: At the June 27, 2023 Regular meeting, the Commission reviewed and
approved five Malibu City Gallery Art Exhibitions for Fiscal Year 2023-24. At the August 8,
2023 Special meeting, the Commission approved an adjustment to the schedule, allowing
Wes Van Dyke as the featured artist for the fall 2023 exhibition. From July 2023 to January
2024, the Commission has curated the following art exhibitions at the Malibu City Gallery,

  •  "Shifting Tides" Community Art Exhibition (June 2023)
  •  "Vistas" by Wes Van Dyke (September 2023)
  •  "Dick Van Dyke - Moments in Time" by Laura Johansen (November 2023)
  •  Malibu Student Art Exhibition (February 2024)

The Commission also approved artist Leigh Mccloskey as the exhibitor from March to May
2024.

By consensus, the Commission requested the Malibu Public Art Exhibitions Ad Hoc
Committee (Ad Hoc Committee), consisting of Vice Chair Lawrence and Commissioner
Holland, return to the Commission in early 2024 to discuss the artist or theme for the
remaining spring exhibition. The Ad Hoc Committee met in January and recommended
Pep Williams as the final featured artist for the Fiscal Year.

At the January 23, 2024 Regular meeting, the Commission did not approve the Ad Hoe's
recommendation. The Commission asked to bring back the item at the February 27, 2024
Regular meeting, and requested additional time to contact artists who could exhibit artwork
following the Leigh McCloskey show. Commissioners were provided a deadline to provide
staff with artists information by February 10, 2024. Staff did not receive any artists

  Page 1 of 2
  Agenda Item# 3.B.2.
 submissions by the deadline; therefore staff recommends the Commission approve the Ad
Hoe's recommendation to feature artist, Pep Williams for the May 2024 art exhibition.

The exhibitions will be open to the public from 8:00 AM to 4:00 PM, Monday through
Friday, at the Malibu City Gallery in City Hall. Funding for the exhibitions, including
marketing, online art call submission fees, and supplies, were included in the Adopted
Budget for Fiscal Year 2023-24. The Ad Hoc Committee will curate and coordinate the
programs related to each exhibition and provide updates during Commission Regular
meetings.

Subject:  Guidelines for Temporary Public Art

RECOMMENDED ACTION: 1) Review the draft guidelines for the temporary display of
artwork; and 2) Provide feedback to staff.

DISCUSSION: At the January 24, 2023 Regular meeting, the Commission discussed
guidelines for temporary public art and requested Commissioner Cherin to work with staff
to draft a Temporary Public Art Guidelines for future discussion.

As part of the initial discussion, the Commission reviewed Council Resolution 17-35, the
implementation guidelines for the Art in Public Places Ordinance, and the Malibu Park
Enhancement and Donation Program. The Ordinance and Guidelines were crafted with
feedback from the Cultural Arts Commission , the Zoning and Ordinance Revisions and
Code Enforcement Subcommittee, and the Planning Commission in 2014.

At the November 28, 2023 Regular meeting , artist David Kramer requested the
Commission to accept his donation of Surfboard Stained Glass, which has been displayed
at Malibu City Hall since December 2022. The Commission denied the donation and
approved a 90-day art loan extension. Additionally, by consensus, the Commission
requested to review and draft guidelines based on the acceptance of temporary artwork
at the next Regular meeting.

Based on Commission feedback during the January 24, 2023 and November 28, 2023
Regular meetings, staff drafted the Malibu Arts Commission Acceptance of Temporary Art
Criteria and Guidelines (Attachment 1). The document also includes the Malibu City
Gallery Temporary Art Collection program approved by the Commission on November 28 ,
2023 Regular meeting.

Staff brought an item to the Commission on January 23, 2024, and by consensus, the
Commission requested to continue the item to the next Regular meeting.

  •  The Malibu Arts Commission will select one artwork from an artist showcased in the Malibu

implementation of guidelines for the Art in Public Places Ordinance under Malibu Municipal Code

RECOMMENDED ACTION: 1) Review the Proposed Malibu Arts Budget for Fiscal Year

DISCUSSION: The City's Annual Budget covers the period of July 1 to June 30 and serves
as a financial guide in providing services to the community based on the City Council's
Annual Work Plan. The operating budget is organized by department, then by program ,
including narratives to explain the program's details, purpose, and goals.

The Malibu Arts Budget (Arts Budget) includes funding for the Poet Laureate program, Art
Exhibitions, Arts in Education, Art Talks, publications, and film previews (Attachment 1).
The Arts Budget is funded from the General Fund Undesignated Reserve, which are funds
used to account for all assets and liabilities not funded through Revenue, County, State,
or Grant funds.

The Proposed Arts Budget for Fiscal Year 2024-25 (Attachment 2) includes art events,
programs, and exhibitions. Additional expenses include culmination projects for the 2023-
25 Poet Laureate, such as a new poetry stone and community anthology, an artist stipend
for the storm drain art project, and a general increase in operating and contractor costs.
The Malibu Arts budget is separated into several categories based on the type of expense.

Salaries & Benefits
Expenditures are related to City personnel, including salaries, benefits, and full and part-
time compensation. The amount of funding allocated to full-time staff in the Arts Budget is
based on the estimated percentage of time spent by staff on arts-related programs.

Contract Personnel
Expenditures for services performed by personnel from temporary agencies or through a
limited contract with the City. These include instructors, performers, vendors, and caterers.
All contract personnel costs related to the Arts in Education program are included in this
section and the Malibu Poet Laureate annual stipend . The budget also includes funding
  Page 1 of 3  Agenda Item # 5.A.
 for musicians to perform at six art exhibitions. Staff are researching options to add the
storm drain art project (Project) to the 2024-25 budget, previously completed in 2019. An
increase of $15,000 includes the artist stipend for the Project.
Current Budget: $30,000
Proposed Budget FY 24-25: $34,900

Travel & Training
Expenditures associated with the professional development of staff and Commissioners,
such as conferences, meetings, and training. Related costs include training registration,
transportation, and lodging.
Current Budget: $1,000
Proposed Budget FY 24-25: $1,000

Dues & Memberships
Expenditures associated with professional memberships or licensing rights. The City
purchases rights for public performance licensing to preview films legally. The licensing
satisfies federal copyright requirements.
Current Budget: $2,800
Proposed Budget FY 24-25: $1,000

Advertising & Noticing
Expenditures associated with arts programming and events related to advertising and
noticing. These include newspaper and virtual advertisements, banners, signs, and other
marketing materials.
Current Budget: $12,000
Proposed Budget FY 24-25: $7,200

Printing
A new FY 2024-25 budget section includes funding for printing art publications, which was
formally listed in the Advertising and Noticing section. The City will produce the annual
Student Poetry and Art Anthology in late 2025. The Community Anthology will be the
Malibu Poet Laureate's culmination project. Additionally, the Commission will review
options to produce an Artist Directory.
Current Budget: $3,500
Proposed Budget FY 24-25: $10,500

Operating Supplies
Expenditures related to general operations of programs and events, including
refreshments, paper supplies, art installation hardware, and other basic supplies. In FY
2024-25 the Poet Laureate will add a new Poetry Stone to Legacy Park. Other additions
include operating the Art Talks program with Santa Monica College, Malibu campus.
Current Budget: $23,500
Proposed Budget FY 24-25: $22,200

Arts in Education program. The City will publish the seventh edition of the Annual Student Poetry
and Art Anthology in FY 2023-24. The Poet Laureate Committee collaborates with community
partners such as the Malibu Library and Pepperdine University to promote literary arts.

Art Exhibitions have included acclaimed artists in addition to displaying community artists in the
Malibu City Gallery located at City Hall. The Arts Commission is working toward exhibiting
exclusive works by world-renowned artists in FY 2023-24.

The Malibu Arts Commission of the City of Malibu does hereby find, order, and resolve as follows:

  SECTION 1. The Malibu Arts Commission does hereby adopt the following Rules of
Procedure and Decorum for the Conduct of Malibu A1ts Commission Meetings:

  1.  RULES FOR COMMISSIONERS

  A.  Decorum
  Members of the Malibu Arts Commission (hereinafter referred to as
  "Commission") shall conduct themselves in an orderly and businesslike
  manner to ensure that the business of the Commission shall be attended to
  efficiently and thoroughly and to ensure that the integrity of the deliberative
  process of the Commission is maintained at all times. Members of the
  Commission shall maintain a polite, respectful, and courteous manner when
  addressing one another, the City staff, and members of the public during
  Commission meetings.

  B.  Election of Officers
  The Commission shall hold an election at its regular meeting in June of each
  year to select a Chair and Vice Chair from its membership. If the full
  Commission is not in attendance, the election shall be continued to the next
  Commission meeting at which all Commissioners are present.

  The Chair and Vice Chair shall remain in office until replaced by newly
  elected officers.

  c.  Role of the Presiding Officer
  The presiding officer of the Commission, who shall be the Chair or, in the
  Chair's absence, the Vice Chair, shall be responsible for maintaining the order
  and decorum of meetings. It shall be the duty of the presiding officer to
  ensure that the Commission's adopted Rules of Procedure and Decorum are
  followed at all times. The presiding officer shall maintain control of
  communication between Commissioners and between the Commission and
  the public and shall chair each meeting in a fair and impartial manner. It shall
  be the duty of each Commissioner to support the presiding officer in
  maintaining the order and decorum of Commission meetings.

  D.  Communication between Commissioners
  Commissioners should request the floor of the presiding officer before
  speaking. Commissioners shall speak in turn, and no Commissioner shall
  speak again until all Commissioners shall have had the opp01tunity to speak.
  Commissioners shall remember that the purpose of the Commission meeting
  is to conduct the bnsiness of the Commission. Commissioners shall avoid

  ATTACHMENT 1

  repetition and shall endeavor to limit their comments to the subject matter at
  hand. Commissioners should endeavor to express their views without
  engaging in lengthy debates. When one Commissioner is speaking, other
  Commissioners shall not interrupt or disturb the speaker. During questions
  and deliberations, the presiding officer shall va1y the speaking sequence of
  Commissioners from item to item.

  E.  Communication with the Public Addressing the Commission
  On specific agenda items, Commissioners may question any person
  addressing the Commission at the conclusion of all public testimony on that
  agenda item before the Commission. Commissioners shall not engage any
  member of the public in a dialogue with themselves, other Commissioners,
  City staff, or other members of the public. All requests to speak shall be
  made to the presiding officer. If a member of the public addresses the
  Commission on a matter not on the meeting's agenda, Commissioners shall
  refrain from a discussion of the matter. Public comments requesting specific
  Commission discussion and/or action shall be summarized by the presiding
  officer following all public comments. Such matters may, at the direction of
  the majority of the City Council or the City Manager, be placed on a future
  agenda for discussion and/or action.

2.  RULES FOR CITY STAFF

  A.  Decorum
  City staff shall not engage in dialogue with members of the public during
  Commission meetings. When addressed by a Commissioner, staff shall
  respond in a polite, respectful and comieous manner. All requests to speak
  shall be made to the presiding officer.

  B.  Role of the City Manager
  The City Manager's duties during Commission meetings are advisory in
  nature.

  RULES FOR THE PUBLIC

  A.  Members of the Audience
  Members of the audience shall not engage in disorderly or boisterous
  conduct, including clapping, whistling, stamping of feet or other acts which
  disturb, disrupt, impede or otherwise disturb the orderly conduct of the
  Commission meeting.

  B.  Persons Addressing the Commission
  Any person wishing to address the Commission on an item before the
  Commission should fill out a speaker slip, which shall include the meeting

  date, name of the speaker, and issue being addressed. The speaker shall
  submit the speaker slip to the Recording Secretary prior to that agenda item
  being announced by the presiding officer. No person shall address the
  Commission without first being recognized by the presiding officer. Members
  of the public addressing the Commission shall have three minutes to speak.
  The Commission may, by majority vote, alter this time limit. Additional
  speakers (who must be present at the time) may surrender their opportunity to

  meeting may, at the discretion of the presiding officer or a majority of the
  Commission, be subject to ejection from that meeting.

  C.  Enforcement
  Upon violation of these Rules, the presiding officer shall request that the
  person violating the rules cease such conduct. If, after a warning from the
  presiding officer, the person persists in disrupting the meeting, the presiding
  officer shall order the person to leave the Commission meeting. Ifthe person
  does not leave the meeting, the presiding officer may order any law
  enforcement officer on duty to act as sergeant-at-arms and remove the person
  from the room in which the Commission meeting is being held. Any person
  who resists removal by the sergeant-at-arms may be charged with a violation
  of these rules, as well as any other applicable ordinance or law. If the
  presiding officer of the Commission fails to enforce these rules, a majority
  vote of the Commission may designate another Commissioner to act as
  presiding officer and enforce these rules. If a meeting of the Commission is
  disturbed in such a manner as to make infeasible the restoration of order, the
